next_steps.title: Physiology-informed personalization challenge
next_steps.purpose: Test whether EEG/EMG improves over the locked kernel_residual_shrink4 personalization baseline.
next_steps.why_now: 05af confirms the personalization baseline; the next physiology test must be stricter and targeted.
next_steps.success_condition: EEG/EMG model beats locked B2 baseline with paired subject-level confirmatory evidence.

next_steps.title: Calibration-sample reduction audit
next_steps.purpose: Test whether EEG/EMG reduces required calibration samples, e.g. k=4 or k=8 matching k=16 personalization.
next_steps.why_now: Even if EEG/EMG does not improve final RMSE, it may be valuable if it reduces subject calibration burden.
next_steps.success_condition: Physiology-assisted lower-k model matches or beats locked k=16 baseline without subject-level instability.

next_steps.title: Failure-subject physiology rescue audit
next_steps.purpose: Focus on subjects where locked personalization still regresses and test whether physiology explains those failures.
next_steps.why_now: 05af failure subjects define the most scientifically useful error surface.
next_steps.success_condition: Physiology improves failure-subject RMSE while preserving pooled and paired metrics.

claim_lock.current_scientific_direction: Personalization-first emotion recognition with physiology as an incremental moderator/challenge, not as an unconstrained zero-shot decoder.
claim_lock.forbidden_claim: Do not claim EEG/EMG success merely because it beats stimulus_only.
claim_lock.required_claim: EEG/EMG must beat the locked personalized baseline or reduce calibration burden with paired subject-level evidence.
